turns.t: Morning, Mr Fitzgerald. I'm Gráinne, I'm the healthcare assistant. I've printed your medication list for the doctor, so we can go through it. ~
Ah, thanks a million. Sure, I'll talk the hind legs off a donkey, you'll have to stop me. ~
Hello, Mr Fitzgerald. It's the back, isn't it, and the leg?
It is, doctor. Lower back, and it runs down the back of my left leg, to the calf, like a hot wire.
How long has that been going on?
Three weeks. It started after I was lifting sacks of potatoes. I'm a farmer, you see.
Is it worse sitting, standing, or walking?
Sitting, mostly. And coughing, or sneezing, that sends a jolt down.
Any numbness, or weakness in the foot?
A bit of tingling in the toes. But the foot's strong. No weakness.
Any trouble with your bladder or bowels, or numbness in your groin? ~
None whatsoever. ~
Doctor, here's his list. ~
Thanks, Gráinne. Mr Fitzgerald, let's go through the medicines.
Naproxen, 500 mg twice a day, with food. And paracetamol, 1 gram, four times a day.
Is that helping? ~
Takes the edge off. Not the leg. ~
Any other conditions?
High blood pressure, and my knees.
Do you smoke?
I stopped a few years back, ten a day, for forty years.
Would you like me to take his blood pressure, doctor? ~
Not today, thanks, Gráinne. Mr Fitzgerald, I'll check your leg. Lift it straight. ~
Ow. That's the one.
It's reproduced the pain when I raise the left leg, and your ankle reflex is a bit reduced on that side, but your strength is normal. ~
Is that a disc? ~
It sounds like sciatica, which is a pinched nerve at the lower back, often from a slipped disc. ~
Will it need surgery? ~
Most people improve without it, over six to twelve weeks. ~
Could I keep working? ~
Yes, gentle activity, but no heavy lifting. Staying in bed is worse.
How will I lift the sacks? ~
Ask for help, and bend your knees. ~
I'll get my son. ~
Keep taking the naproxen with food, and the paracetamol regularly.
And hot water bottles, doctor? ~
Heat helps, yes. If you develop numbness between your legs, can't control your bladder or bowels, or your foot becomes weak, go to the emergency department right away.
I will. ~
Otherwise, if it's not better in six weeks, come back and I'll arrange a scan and a physiotherapy referral.
Right. Thanks a million, doctor. ~
